newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra approves MBF insurance rate change.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra approves MBF insurance rate change.

text.p: The Australian government on Wednesday approved rate changes for health insurers with Medical Benefits Fund of Australia (MBF), the Fund said.
The Fund would offer a new pricing structure from February, minimising increases in health insurance fees and, in many cases, reducing the cost of private health cover, the Fund said.
Members could increase levels of health cover by choosing from a wide range of excess packages, benefitting from the government's tax rebates which take effect from July 1, it said.
"Under the new pricing structure it will be possible for many families to obtain health cover for around A$1,000 and still be eligible for the government's tax rebate," it said in a statement.

In the 1996/97 (July-June) budget the Liberal-National government announced tax incentives worth A$500 million a year to encourage people to take out private health insurance and to wean rich people off the public Medicare health system.
The Fund anticipated a rise in contribution rates of 6.5 percent across its membership.
